title: D-087 PDF-reading P3 (the M5-T113 real-corpus next blockers): per-page work budgets under a bounded document ceiling (DB-055 c), the sh shading operator skipped as non-geometry, inline images (BI/ID/EI) skipped safely instead of refusing the document (DB-055 d) - re-run the six real architect PDFs by sha256
objective: Take the architect-sheet reader past the three named blockers from the M5-T113 corpus run. (1) Budgets (DB-055 c): items 1-2 (88- and 94-page vector sets) hit the per-DOCUMENT 200k operator budget; restructure the point/operator/decoded-byte budgets as per-PAGE budgets under a bounded per-document ceiling (declare every number and the worst-case CPU/memory arithmetic; nothing unbounded; the per-request deadline stays the future route's duty, DB-076 d). (2) The sh operator (ISO 32000-1 8.7.4.2 / Table 77 area, shading) paints a colour fill, not linework: skip it as non-geometry with a disclosure count, never a refusal (item 3). (3) Inline images (8.9.7: BI <dict> ID <data> EI) are skipped safely instead of refusing the whole document (item 4): parse the inline image dictionary with the existing bounded lexer, compute the data length when it is determinable (unfiltered: width x height x components x bits), otherwise scan for a whitespace-delimited EI under a byte cap; any ambiguity = a typed refusal, never a guess that desynchronizes the content stream. Put the inline-image logic in a new module app/drawings/sheet_inline_image.py so sheet_interpreter.py (690 lines) stays under 750. Then re-run the six real files by sha256 and report honestly: if any reads fully, say which and what it produced; items 5-6 are scans and stay an honest scan-only refusal.
